title: Joint vs independent control with leakage matched to a real GPU's measured temperature slope
research_question: Does joint control keep its advantage over independent control when the simulator's leakage is only as temperature-sensitive as measured on real hardware?
hypothesis: H1: with leakage matched to the measured slope (matched_k0.02), joint's advantage over independent is smaller in magnitude than with registry leakage in all 6 scenarios (seed-paired change in joint/independent - 1, 95% CI entirely above 0). H2: with matched leakage (matched_k0.02), joint vs independent energy per successful task lies within the 1% practical threshold in all 6 scenarios (95% CI entirely inside -1%..+1%). H3: H2 also holds for every matched variant (kappa 0.01, 0.02, 0.03, and both ends of the slope's 95% CI). H4: in every scenario where independent control spent chip-seconds above the 80 C target with registry leakage, it spends fewer with matched leakage.
null_hypothesis: Matching leakage to the measured slope leaves joint control's advantage unchanged.
independent_variables: leakage variant (registry; matched at kappa 0.01/0.02/0.03; matched at the slope's CI ends)
baseline: registry_leakage variant within E009 (same seeds and workloads)
configuration: Target: the simulator's relative temperature slope of chip power at s = 0.747, 55.0 C, compute-bound work, set to the measured 0.1346%/K (95% CI 0.1050-0.1642%/K) from M001's warm-up at 1995 MHz, one clock step, constant fan (0.177 +/- 0.039 W/K at 131 W). The registry gives 0.3663%/K at the same point. For each kappa, p_leak_ref is solved to hit the target. Clock sensitivity from M001: {'beta_compute': 0.983, 'beta_memory': 0.0}.
evaluation_criteria: Paired relative differences with 95% t-CI over 5 seeds; practical threshold 1%. H1: per scenario and seed, d = (joint/independent - 1) in the matched variant minus the same in registry_leakage. H4 on seed means of chip-seconds above target.
known_limitations: The target comes from GPU board power of one consumer card over a 4 K window at one operating point; the simulator's slope at other clocks and temperatures follows its exponential model. Several matched p_leak_ref values lie below the registry range swept in E002. The voltage-frequency form is still the rejected registry placeholder. 5 seeds.
disclosure: E002's one-at-a-time results were known when these hypotheses were written: joint vs independent was -0.62% at registry values, -0.04% with p_leak_ref = 30 W and -0.03% with kappa_leak = 0.005, which motivated H2. The measured slopes (M001 warm-up, M002 warm-up) were known. No E009 cells were run before registration.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
